meta.rule: A factor enters the yield only with a published number read from the source itself; anything else stays a notice or a stated input. Nothing is tuned to the documented drought events. Opt-in: with no `factors` option every existing result is reproduced unchanged.

factorTable.factor: Heat at flowering, maize and tomato
factorTable.enters: yield (opt-in): mean daily pollination coefficient over the flowering window multiplies the water-limited relative yield

numbers.shape: logistic, 1 -> 0 over 5 C beyond the threshold
numbers.steepnessNote: our choice: the source gives the shape and the ends, not the steepness

factorTable.source: AquaCrop Reference Manual v7.3 (FAO), Annex I (I.2 Maize 4.2 p.11; I.9 Tomato 4.2; Table 15 beans p.59) and Chapter 3, 3.12.5, Fig. 3.12k p.3-147; read from the PDF
factorTable.simplification: AquaCrop applies the coefficient to the reference harvest index; here the window mean multiplies the relative yield

factorTable.factor: Heat, beans, coffee and the other crops
factorTable.note: Table 15 (dry beans) gives no pollination thresholds; coffee arabica has an optimum annual mean of 18-21 C and quality loss above 23 C (DaMatta & Ramalho 2006) but no yield loss per degree
factorTable.source: AquaCrop Reference Manual v7.3 (FAO), Annex I (I.2 Maize 4.2 p.11; I.9 Tomato 4.2; Table 15 beans p.59) and Chapter 3, 3.12.5, Fig. 3.12k p.3-147; read from the PDF

factorTable.caveat: Africa, not Central America; linear and unbounded here, which is far outside the trial range for long hot cycles

heat.rule: If the heat factor changes the relative yield by more than 0.01 in fewer than 1 % of site-years, nothing is retrained (fixed before seeing the result).

meta.years: 2001-2024 agricultural years with all rain days present (ERA5), cycle completing inside the agricultural year
meta.factor: AquaCrop v7.3 Annex I thresholds (Tmax 40 C, Tmin 10 C) with the logistic fall over 5 C (ch. 3, 3.12.5); mean daily coefficient over the flowering window multiplies the water-limited relative yield (our simplification: AquaCrop applies it to the harvest index); logistic steepness k = 10 is our choice.
meta.rule: If the heat factor changes the relative yield by more than 0.01 in fewer than 1 % of site-years, nothing is retrained (fixed before seeing the result).
meta.lobellSensitivity: Lobell et al. 2011 (Africa): 1 % per degree-day above 30 C (1.7 % under drought; drought here = water-limited relative yield < 0.7), degree-days approximated from daily Tmax over the whole cycle. A proxy from another continent; off by default and never used in decisions.

retrained.reason: 5 of 935 maize site-years (0.53 %) change by more than 0.01, below the 1 % rule; 0 days of flowering windows reach Tmax above 40 C in 20 points x 24 years x 2 cycles, and all 29 affected site-years are cold nights (Tmin below 10 C) at the highland points; the factor is implemented but inactive for heat in this region and these years.

realEvents.method: scripts/compare/real_events_check.mjs (ERA5), same fixed thresholds (hit = worst third), nothing tuned; --heat adds the maize heat factor; fertility not stated; beans unchanged (no threshold)

meta.network: v3 funnel MLP (backprop), seeds 17/29/43, web/data/emulator_v3_mlp_seed{17,29,43}.json; not retrained (the heat factor is almost never active, see factors_heat_counts.json)
meta.method: predict then choose: the network predicts the relative yield of each of 7 crops (resown at the actual date) in the past years; the choice applies the priority (typical = median, cautious = 20th percentile) and the stated constraint. Truth = simulator in year Y (water only).

cases.years2019_2024: 54 cases (3 pilots x years 2019-2024 x loss day 30/45/60)

meta.canResowFalse: Stated constraint, not a prediction: only "leave the field" remains (value 0). The rule baseline and every policy then also get 0 because nothing can be resown.
meta.fertility: What-if: AquaCrop table 2.13a relative biomass (near-optimal 0.80, moderate 0.60, about half 0.50, poor 0.40, very poor 0.25) multiplies the predicted relative yield of every resown crop; the truth is multiplied the same way. Generic classes, not calibrated for Guatemala; there is no source that maps fertilised/not fertilised to a class.
meta.utilityNote: Values are relative yield (0 to 1); no money and no margin.

meta.rule: If the anthracnosis notice is active because of water stress (Ks < 1 on more than half of the last 28 days) the irrigation priority becomes "protect the crop" (price 1 day of stress avoided) whatever the grower stated; roya-only or no notice leaves the priority as stated. Approved in principle by the owner.
meta.decision: irrigate 20 mm today if the predicted stress days avoided (exported network web/data/coffee_ptc_mlp.json, seed 29) exceed the price (3 days = save water, 1 day = protect the crop); the FAO-56 rule irrigates when the capped running depletion exceeds p = 0.40 of the available water and does not use the priority, so the notice rule cannot change it
meta.noticeDays: days in t+1..t+30 with the anthracnosis notice active by stress (share of Ks<1 days over the last 28 days > 0.5), recomputed day by day from the soil water balance with and without the 20 mm irrigation at the end of day t (neverIrrigate/alwaysIrrigate are the two counterfactual series; the policy rows pick the one its decision leads to, per scenario)
meta.rainAndMinador: Roya "favorable" and minador "probable" days in t+1..t+30 depend only on the weather, not on irrigation; they are reported next to the anthracnosis days and do not change any decision.

modes.protectCrop: priority stated = protect the crop, price 1
modes.saveWaterWithNoticeRule: priority stated = save water, raised to protect the crop when anthracnosis-by-stress is active at the decision day

meta.caveat: Notices are information with a source, not damage predictions; the number of notice days is a measure of water stress, not of disease. Scenarios of different shade/soil at one site-year share the weather.

notComputed: Pest damage: no source gives a damage function (the 16 % fall of Central American coffee production in 2013 is a regional aggregate); pests do not change the yield.
Fertiliser response in Guatemala: no published fertilised vs unfertilised number; only the generic AquaCrop classes, stated by the user.
Margin: no production costs, no seed cost, no usable attainable yields; prices are wholesale, not farm-gate.
Heat for beans and coffee: no threshold or loss per degree in the sources.
Cutworm (cogollero) and the other pests: only search snippets, not verified, not used.
decisionMethod: One method: predict then choose (the backprop funnel network predicts the outcome of each option; the choice applies the priority and the stated constraints). The evolutionary recommender is archived as is, not trained or extended.
